title: Morph
description: One black pill on warm white that is the whole player. It plays four records whose sleeves are drawn, not photographed: flat colour, one geometric idea and a small flush-left credit each, a halftone on vermilion, a doorway on cobalt, a hairline on stone, bars on yellow, so the sleeve and the type column beside it speak one Swiss, letterpress language. At rest it is a capsule with the sleeve, the elapsed time and a waveform tinted from the record. Click it and two objects carry the open on one spring: the cover grows out of its own corner from a thumbnail into a sleeve, and the pill's small elapsed time rises beside it and grows, redrawn as real type at every size with the tracking that size calls for, into the headline figures of a flush-left type column. Open, there is no app chrome, only the sleeve and the type. The figures are the scrubber: drag them sideways to seek, and each tabular figure rolls on its own spring like an odometer drum, cut off at the figures' own baseline; only the lead figure leaves the tabular grid when it is a 1, drawn as the face's footless proportional 1, and the colon is spaced optically, ink to ink, measured across its own dots, so the gap from the 1's stem to the dots equals the gap from the dots to the 2's bowl, and both equal the gap the face sets inside '23'; it is recomputed every frame from the figures either side, so it holds as the wheels roll. The type column is exactly as wide as the figures, ink to ink, so they own the measure and the panel follows it as the minutes turn: progress is a single hairline of its own, 8px under the figures' baseline, from the first figure to the last, played in full ink and the rest in the panel's own secondary ink, and the time left stands under its far end on the title's baseline; tap the sleeve to pause, and the colon blinks like a stopped clock. A few seconds before a song ends the pill reshapes on its own into a wider toast announcing the next one, its thumbnail already the next record's sleeve, then folds back. Nothing is a new sheet: width, height and corner radius run on one spring from wherever they are, so you can change your mind mid-morph; the waveform folds flat in place and goes, everything else fades through a slight blur as the edge reveals or absorbs it, and the corners stay continuous curves from capsule to squircle.
intent: Translate the one-surface morph of Emil Kowalski's Dynamic Island recreation (https://emilkowal.ski/ui/dynamic-island) and Family's dynamic tray (https://benji.org/family-values) into a now-playing control: states are shapes of one object on interruptible springs, shared elements travel, the rest crossfades with blur so nothing pops.
